utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-97-24-A --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you --sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I please have the appearances for the parties. First the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRACOL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Good afternoon, Your Honour. Xavier Tracol on behalf of the Prosecution, together with Ms. Helen Brady and Susan Grogan, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Branko Lukic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stakic, I wanted to make sure you can understand us in a language hat you can understand. Can you hear us? Can you understand us?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I can hear you and I understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stakic. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you all for being here this afternoon. This is, as you know, a Status Conference convened in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires that a Status Conference be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. Our last Status Conference in this case was held on the 27th of July, 2004. Mr. Stakic, I would like to turn to you and to ask you whether you have any matters, any issues, that you would like to raise in relation to your detention and in particular whether you have any concerns regarding your mental and physical well-being that I should know about.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for your concern. At this point, I do not have any problems whatsoever nor physical or psychological.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stakic. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: At the moment there is only one motion pending in this appeal. This is a motion by Mr. Stakic under Rule 115 to submit supplementary evidence on appeal. The filing on this motion are now complete, but I am not in a position today to inform you as to the date on which you may expect a decision. But I can assure you all that the Chamber will address it at the earliest possible moment. At this stage I would like to ask the parties whether they wish to raise any other issues. The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRACOL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. No question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. The Defence has nothing to raise today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So if there are no other issues I would like to thank the parties for their attendance, and I would call these proceedings to a close. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: adjourned at 2.34 p.m.
